title: Imran Khan Ends 11-Year Wait, Confirms Bollywood Comeback With Netflix Film Adhure Hum Adhure Tum
excerpt: The Jaane Tu star returns to a leading role with a mature romantic dramedy that draws from his own life, co-starring Bhumi Pednekar and directed by Break Ke Baad's Danish Aslam.
body:
• Actor Imran Khan is returning to a leading role after an 11-year break with Adhure Hum Adhure Tum, a romantic dramedy directed by Danish Aslam and co-starring Bhumi Pednekar.
  • The Netflix film, described as a mature story exploring love, separation, and emotional growth, draws heavily from Khan's own life experiences.
  • Originally slated for early 2026, the film was postponed due to leadership changes at the streaming platform and is now expected later this year.
  • Khan previously made a cameo in Vir Das's Happy Patel: Khatarnak Jasoos in early 2026, his first on-screen appearance since Katti Batti in 2015.

Imran Khan has not led a film since Katti Batti in 2015. Eleven years later, the actor who once defined a generation of urban romantic comedies is preparing his return — not on the big screen, but through Netflix. Adhure Hum Adhure Tum, a romantic dramedy co-starring Bhumi Pednekar, marks Khan's full-fledged comeback to acting.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wxqpCPntOGQ

A Story Close to Home

The film reunites Khan with director Danish Aslam, who last worked with him on Break Ke Baad in 2010. Adhure Hum Adhure Tum is being described as a "dysfunctional romantic dramedy" — a mix of romance, drama, and offbeat humour that explores themes of love, marriage, separation, and emotional growth. Multiple reports indicate the story draws heavily from Khan's own life experiences during his decade away from films.

"We consciously crafted Adhure Hum Adhure Tum to cater to these under-represented ideas," Khan said in a recent interview. "I do feel like there are certain emotional notes that are largely unrepresented in movies nowadays; there's a distinct lack of empathy, kindness and responsibility in our stories and characters."

Why It Took This Long

Khan's disappearance from Bollywood was one of the industry's more puzzling exits. After debuting to massive success with Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na in 2008, he became synonymous with relatable urban characters through films like Delhi Belly, I Hate Luv Storys, and Mere Brother Ki Dulhan. But after Katti Batti underperformed in 2015, Khan stepped away entirely.

His return has been gradual. He first appeared in a cameo in Happy Patel: Khatarnak Jasoos, a spy-comedy directed by and starring Vir Das that released theatrically in early 2026. The film was produced by uncle Aamir Khan's production house. But Adhure Hum Adhure Tum is the real test — his first lead role in over a decade.

A Delayed Release

Shooting wrapped in Mumbai, but the release hit a snag. The film was originally slated for early 2026 on Netflix, but leadership changes at the streaming platform disrupted the content calendar. According to HT City, the executive overseeing the project left the platform, pushing the entire slate. The makers are now targeting a release window in the second half of 2026, with the film currently in post-production.

Khan has also chosen Netflix deliberately. In an interview, he pushed back against Bollywood's current obsession with box-office tracking, comparing it to a sport played "with spreadsheets and calculators." He described Adhure Hum Adhure Tum as "a gentle, relationship story" better suited to streaming than the theatrical marketplace.

What to Watch For

Gurfateh Pirzada plays a key supporting role alongside Pednekar, who has established herself as one of Hindi cinema's most versatile actors. For diaspora audiences who grew up watching Khan's early work, the comeback carries a particular nostalgia. Whether a decade of absence has sharpened or blunted his appeal is the question the film will answer.
